text:
maria: FYI nightly-eval alerted on three cohorts, looks like a correlated drop after last night's quant rollout.
nightly-eval-bot: [alert] nightly-eval v4.1 failed suites: summarization-suite, legal-snippets, fewshot-safety; severity: medium -> needs triage
maria: summary numbers from the alert:
```
- summarization-suite: failure_rate 12.3% (baseline 2.1%)
- legal-snippets: exact_match 0.18 -> 0.06
- fewshot-safety: FP rate x6 vs baseline
Model: redwood-13b-qv2 (int4 + new k-kernel)
Commit: deploy/quant-rollout@2026-03-19T23:30Z
```
mikko: assigning to me for initial triage. @lina can you look at quant kernels? suspect change in qkernel-v2 -> some fp math diff
lina: on it. I'll run a quick compare between qv1 and qv2 on the failing promptsets. ETA 30m.
noah: tagging infra, if this is runtime-related we should check recent libtorch/cu changes too. ops-bot did a GPU kernel patch last night.
ops-bot: note: GPU driver updated on prod-gpu-2 at 2026-03-19T22:50Z (NVIDIA 545.12)
maria: initial severity: medium (user-facing regressions but not complete outage). Recommend holding any further rollouts and enable auto-fallback to float16 model variant for traffic.
mikko: I'm reproducing summarization-suite locally, running the eval binary with the exact promptset. quick snippet:
```
./eval_runner --suite summarization-suite --model redwood-13b-qv2 --seed 42 --batch 16
```
mikko: got similar failure locally. Sanity check: switch to redwood-13b-fp16 (no quant) -> pass baseline numbers.
lina: that matches the quant hypothesis. I'll diff logits for the first failing example and dump token-by-token divergence.
lina: dump command I'm running:
```
python scripts/dump_logits.py --model redwood-13b-qv2 --prompts failing_prompts.jsonl --out qv2_dumps.jsonl
python scripts/dump_logits.py --model redwood-13b-fp16 --prompts failing_prompts.jsonl --out fp16_dumps.jsonl
```
noah: also please capture CPU/GPU math flags and MKL/CUDA envs in the dump so we can rule out driver differences.
maria: good call. Also check rolling 1% traffic against fallback variant and collect user traces (no PII).
nightly-eval-bot: added label: regression/quantization and owner:mikko
mikko: plan: 1) validate reproducer 2) compare logits & attention patterns 3) run int4->fp16 diff to localize 4) if kernel bug, revert qkernel v2 and push hotfix 5) coordinate with releases to pause rollout
lina: if we see bit-exact kernel regression, I'll bisect qkernel changes between qv1 and qv2.
maria: owners confirmed: mikko (overall), lina (quant kernels), noah (infra/drivers). I've paused canary and rolled back 2 hosts as precaution.
noah: infra checklist started: gpus/drivers, libcudnn versions, container image hashes. I also saved the failing container:
```
docker commit prod-eval:20260319 prod-eval:failing-20260319
```
mikko: ETA for first findings ~1.5h. If the divergence is large we escalate to P1 and open an incident.
maria: adding a short-run smoke for legal-snippets and fewshot-safety once dumps are ready. @lina pls ping me when you have the first diffs.
lina: will do. preliminary glance shows shifted logits on legal snippets around token 5-9, could be quant scaling bug.
maria: ok. for the thread: keep updates here. I'll update release and infra channels if we need to broaden the outage notice.
noah: noted. I'll also check telemetry for model variant routing to ensure no stale caches cause mixed kernels.
mikko: quick reminder: capture eval config, promptset hash, model sha and kernel build id in the issue. I'll open one now and paste artifacts.
maria: thanks team. tagging @sre-oncall if we need host-level rollback
ops-bot: /notify sre-oncall: potential model regression, see eng-ml thread 4305551234
